payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image show a basketball playing surface as part of the background?
node.criteria: Pass if a recognizable basketball playing surface is visible in the background; fail if the background is visibly not a basketball playing surface; unknown if the background or its surface cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Assess the background relative to the input image and requested replacement. A visible playing surface is evidence toward the requested basketball-court background, not by itself proof that the full change is complete.

node_traces.evidence: The background shows a basketball hoop and balls, but the visible surface is a plain, featureless dark area rather than a recognizable basketball playing surface.

fulfillment: The binding is too vague and the aggregate incorrectly treats conflicting support as cumulative proof: the edited image shows a hoop, balls, and a court line, but the large dark background is not clearly a recognizable playing surface. Preserve the distinction between complete and partial progress: equipment alone can establish progress, not completion when the surface/court context is absent or ambiguous. Reconcile the supports against the image and original request rather than letting one positive support override the other; explicitly assess whether the background itself reads as a court. Keep uncertainty available when evidence cannot resolve that criterion. This is a semantic evidence/aggregation issue, not a transport or schema failure.
s2: The node correctly detects basketball equipment and court markings, so retain it as evidence of progress. Its binding should not let equipment alone stand in for the requested background transformation: the edited image has a hoop, balls, and a court line, but most of the background is a featureless dark field rather than a clearly recognizable basketball-court setting. Make the support explicitly distinguish visible basketball-related evidence from evidence that the background itself reads as a court, and ensure downstream fulfillment combines this support with the completion criterion rather than treating a pass here as proof of completion. Preserve unknown when the relevant background context is genuinely unassessable; do not turn ambiguity into a negative. This is a semantic evidence/criterion issue, not a transport or schema failure.

response.content: {"text":"The binding already limits this support to evidence of a playing surface, not proof of full completion; preserve that distinction. The trace’s confident failure appears to overlook the edited image’s bright court floor and visible court line beneath the subject, alongside the hoop and basketballs. Make the assessment attend to the whole background and count recognizable surface cues even when much of the backdrop is dark; do not require the entire background to look like a court. Keep unknown for genuinely unassessable surfaces, and leave overall completion to the fulfillment logic. This is a visual-evidence/criterion calibration issue, not a transport or schema failure."}
